title: A field guide for coaches
intro: Let students explore, make a claim, and look for evidence that could change their minds.

sections.title: A short first visit
paragraphs: Spend five minutes changing the growth controls. Compare a mat with a floating bloom. Ask what the drawing cannot tell us.
Spend ten minutes at Detect or Identify. Save one finding and one uncertainty. Finish by sharing a question your team could test.

sections.title: Return with a new question
paragraphs: Each station has four challenges. Progress stays on this browser. There is no speed score or leaderboard. Students can revisit completed challenges with new settings.
Ask: What is real here? What is invented? Where and when was this sampled? What evidence would make your claim stronger?

sections.title: Keep the team’s idea their own
paragraphs: The project prompts ask students to define their own next test. Do not treat the game choices or model inputs as a finished FLL solution.
Export the notebook before changing devices. Students should explain which notes are their ideas and which plots are simulated.

sections.title: Local science to review
paragraphs: Lady Bird Lake is a narrow, dammed river reach. Benthic mats can be hidden below the surface and later float up. Clear water, an image or a pigment reading cannot establish safety.
Real toxin records are sparse and heterogeneous. Taxonomic names for the local study image plates remain unassigned here. Review these limits with Chintan before classroom claims or a presentation.
